stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 6 - (x - 3)^{2}\). What is the maximum value of \(f(x)\)?
solution: \((x - 3)^{2}\) is never negative, and it equals \(0\) when \(x = 3\).
So \(f(x) = 6 - (x - 3)^{2}\) is at most \(6\), and \(f(3) = 6\). The maximum value is \(6\).
verify:
x = symbols('x')
f = 6 - (x - 3)**2
xv = solve(diff(f, x), x)[0]
assert diff(f, x, 2) < 0 and f.subs(x, xv) == 6
assert [Rational(s) for s in spr_answers] == [6]
